description: Simulates the Resend email API: single and batch sends with idempotency keys and scheduling (reschedule and cancel), reading and listing emails with cursor pagination, test-address outcomes, domains (create, read, update, verify, delete), API keys (create, list, rename, delete, sending_access and domain-bound), webhooks (register, read, update, delete) with Svix-signed delivery of email and domain events, and the audiences, audience contacts and broadcasts routes the SDKs call.

lifecycle.changelog:
Follow-up to 0.1.0, released 2026-02-18. It fixes how the emulator answers the calls 0.1.0 served and extends it to the 21 Resend operations of transactional email: sending, scheduling, domains, API keys and webhooks. It targets the Resend API as documented and as Resend's sandbox answered in November 2026, and the official SDKs resend-go v4.7.0 (0.1.0 targeted v2), resend-node 6.30.0 and resend-python 2.48.0. Resend does not version its API.

### What changed since 0.1.0
- Sending: to, cc, bcc and reply_to accept a string or an array, up to 50 recipients. Batch sends cap at 100 and follow x-batch-validation: strict fails the whole batch on one invalid email, permissive sends the valid ones and returns the errors. Idempotency-Key replays the first answer for 24 hours and answers 409 when the body changes. Sending from a domain you created and have not verified answers 403
- Test addresses settle as Resend's do: delivered@, bounced@, complained@ and suppressed@resend.dev, with +label on the first three
- Reading back: GET /emails/{id} returns Resend's fields (message_id, tags, scheduled_at, text from html), and GET /emails lists sent emails newest first with cursor pagination (limit, after, before)
- Scheduling: scheduled_at takes ISO 8601 or "in N min|hour|day", up to 30 days ahead. PATCH /emails/{id} reschedules and POST /emails/{id}/cancel cancels. A scheduled email goes out when its time passes on the emulator clock (advance it through /admin/time/advance)
- Domains: create, read, list, update, verify and delete, with Resend's DNS records, capabilities and tracking switches. Verify settles on verified by default; /admin/config can make it pending or failed
- API keys: create, list, rename and delete. A sending_access key may only send, and a key bound to a domain is refused when it sends from that domain while it is unverified
- Webhooks: register, read, list, update and delete endpoints, each with a whsec_ signing secret. Sends and domain changes deliver email.* and domain.* events signed the way Resend signs them, which resend.webhooks.verify accepts in all three SDKs. /admin/emails/{id}/events/{event} triggers email.opened, clicked, delivery_delayed and failed on demand
- Behaviour changes for 0.1.0 callers: ids are UUIDs (email ids are time-ordered), not email_000001. Errors are JSON {statusCode, name, message} with the HTTP status equal to statusCode, and every route needs a key before anything else is checked. created_at reads in Resend's Postgres form. Lists answer {object: list, has_more, data}, with data [] when empty. Responses carry Resend's ratelimit-* headers

### Supported
- 21 Resend operations: POST /emails, POST /emails/batch, GET /emails, GET /emails/{id}, PATCH /emails/{id}, POST /emails/{id}/cancel; domains (6); API keys (4); webhooks (5)
- The legacy audiences, audience contacts and broadcasts routes the SDKs still call, kept as in 0.1.0
- State snapshots, reset, seeding and a controllable clock through /admin

### Verified
- Official SDKs resend-go v4.7.0, resend-node 6.30.0 and resend-python 2.48.0: 61 of 61 scenario cases against this build
- Through LocalStack: 61 of 61 cases with this build, with webhook receivers reachable from the container
- Live comparison with Resend: not run for this build

### Not modelled
- Any non-empty Bearer token is accepted; only keys created through the emulator carry restrictions
- Sending from a domain the emulator has never seen is accepted; strict_sender_domains in /admin/config refuses every unverified domain, as Resend does
- Rate limits are off by default (an /admin/config switch turns on 429s); email quotas are not kept
- Absolute natural-language times such as "tomorrow at 9am" answer 422
- Webhook retries are three attempts one second apart; Resend's day-long schedule, endpoint auto-disable, event replay and secret rotation are not served. Webhook endpoints may use http, which Resend refuses
- Opens, clicks, delays and failures happen only through the admin trigger
- Templates, segments, topics, top-level contacts, receiving and inbound email are not served. Every deliberate difference from Resend is listed in twin-resend/divergences.json

### Known issues
- tracking_subdomain is accepted on domain create and update and not kept
- The legacy audiences, contacts and broadcasts lists return every item and ignore limit, after and before
- A just-scheduled email can be cancelled at once; Resend refuses for about a second after the send
